review.why: Install a Claude Code PreToolUse hook that blocks destructive git commands such as push, reset --hard, clean -f and branch -D.
review.summary: A short setup guide plus a 25-line bash hook. It asks for project or global scope, copies the script, merges a PreToolUse hook into settings.json, offers to edit the blocked patterns and gives a one-line test that should exit with code 2. Matching is a plain pattern check on the command string.
strengths: Does one thing and ends with a test command that proves the hook works.
Tells the agent to merge into existing settings instead of overwriting them.
The script is tiny and readable, so the blocked list is easy to adjust.
cautions: The script needs jq and bash, which the skill does not mention; on Windows both must be available to the hook shell.
It blocks every git push by default, and string matching can be bypassed (for example git -C dir push); it is a guardrail, not a security boundary.
SKILL.md and the script read in full; not run here.
